Collison played four seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He earned [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] conference honors three times, and won the [[Frances Pomeroy Naismith Award]] his senior year as the top college player standing {{convert|6|ft|0|in|m}} or under. He was drafted by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in the first round with the 21st overall pick of the [[2009 NBA draft]]. Collison also played for the [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Sacramento Kings]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. ==Early life== Collison was born in [[Rancho Cucamonga, California]] to parents Dennis and [[June Griffith]], who were both elite track and field athletes for [[Guyana]]. As a senior at [[Etiwanda High School]] under coach Dave Kleckner, Collison was named a fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].{{cite web | title= Player Bio: Darren Collison | publisher= UCLA | url=http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1013 | access-date=September 2, 2016}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Collison was listed as the No. 16 point guard and the No. 100 player in the nation in 2005.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Darren-Collison-29729;_ylt=AifpKrlzUoRjuVZqu_XZbLdGPZB4 Darren Collison Recruiting Profile] ==College career== [[File:Darren-Collison-UCLA-vs-DePaul-12-13-08.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Collison with UCLA in 2008]] He was a backup to [[Jordan Farmar]] in the [[2005–06 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|Bruins' 2005–06 season]], becoming the starting [[point guard]] the following season. He was awarded the MVP of the [[Maui Invitational Tournament]] in December 2006 and was named the [[Pacific-10 Conference]] Player of the Week on December 4, 2006, and again on February 18, 2007. During the [[2006–07 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2006–07 season]], Collison averaged 2.2 steals per game—the most in the [[Pacific-10 Conference]]. He also averaged 5.7 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] (2nd in the Pac-10), as well as a [[three-point field goal]] percentage of 44.7 percent.{{Cite web |url=http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2006-2007/teamcume.html |title=UCLA Official Athletic Site – Men's Basketball |access-date=November 6, 2007 |archive-date=September 7, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907192910/http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2006-2007/teamcume.html |url-status=dead }} Collison returned to UCLA for his junior and senior years and ended up playing in a total of 142 games at UCLA, tied for the most ever. In his senior year in [[2008–09 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008–09]], he was named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 team]] after averaging 14.4 points, 4.7 assists, and 1.6 steals per game. He led the conference in free throw percentage, and was third in assists, steals, and assists-to-turnover ratio. Collison won the [[Frances Pomeroy Naismith Award]] that year, awarded to the best college player 6 ft 0 in (1.83 m) or shorter.{{cite news|last=Rose |first=Adam |title=UCLA's Darren Collison receives (2009–2010)=== Collison was widely considered to be one of the top [[point guard]] prospects in the 2009 NBA Draft coming out of UCLA.{{cite web|title=Draft Watch: Getting to the point|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=FordDraftWatch-090115|website=ESPN.go.com|date = January 15, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=February 20, 2009}} He was selected in the first round with the 21st overall pick by the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Collison Picked 21st by the New Orleans Hornets in the NBA draft|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2009/06/25/collison-picked-21st-new-orleans-hornets-nba-draft|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215021224/https://pac-12.com/article/2009/06/25/collison-picked-21st-new-orleans-hornets-nba-draft|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 15, 2020|website=Pac-12.com|publisher= Pac-12 Conference|date=June 25, 2009|access-date=February 14, 2020}} With [[Chris Paul]] out for months at two separate times during the 2009–10 season, Collison became the starting point guard. Collison handed out a Hornets rookie-record 18 assists and scored 17 points on January 30, 2010, when New Orleans ended Memphis's 11-game home winning streak with a 113–111 overtime victory. Later on March 8, 2010, Collison broke his own record with a Hornets rookie-record 20 assists (along with 16 points) in a 135–131 victory over the Golden State Warriors. In a game against the Indiana Pacers on February 19, 2010, Collison became only the second rookie of the 2009–10 season to get a triple-double with 18 points, 13 rebounds, and 12 assists. He finished 4th in the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting and averaged 18.8 points and 9.1 assists in the 37 games as a starter, but had four turnovers a contest as a starter in his first NBA season. ===Indiana Pacers (2010–2012)=== [[File:Darren Collison Dunk.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Collison with the Pacers in May 2012]] On August 11, 2010, the Hornets traded Collison and [[James Posey]] to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in a four-team, five-player deal that also sent [[Troy Murphy]] to the [[New Jersey Nets]], [[Trevor Ariza]] to the New Orleans Hornets and [[Courtney Lee]] to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|title=Pacers get Collison from Hornets in 4-team trade|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt1|website=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2010|access-date=August 11, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530080120/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/11/four.team.trade.ap/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt1|archive-date=May 30, 2011|df=mdy-all}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2012–2013)=== On July 12, 2012, Collison and [[Dahntay Jones]] were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[Ian Mahinmi]].{{cite web|title=It's Official: Pacers Trade Mahinmi for Collison, Jones|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/its-official-pacers-acquire-mahinmi-trade-collison-jones|website=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2012|access-date=July 12, 2012}} Collison became the Mavericks' starting point guard, replacing [[Jason Kidd]] who left as a free agent. Collison was a key player in Dallas' 4–1 start in [[2012–13 Dallas Mavericks season|2012–13]], but he struggled as they lost 8 of their next 11. After starting the team's first 14 games, Collison came off the bench for one game.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Caplan|title=Adding Fisher Illustrates Mavs' Deep Flaws At Point Guard|url=http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/2012/11/29/adding-fisher-illustrates-mavs-deep-flaws-at-point-guard/|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2012|access-date=November 29, 2012|url-status=live|df=mdy}} 14 games later, on December 27, 2012, he regained the starting job. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2013–2014)=== [[File:Darren Collison 20131118 Clippers v Grizzles.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Collison with the Clippers in 2013]] On July 10, 2013, Collison signed a deal with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=CLIPPERS SIGN MATT BARNES, DARREN COLLISON, RYAN HOLLINS AND CHRIS PAUL|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-matt-barnes-darren-collison-ryan-hollins-and-chris-paul|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 10, 2013}} He again backed up Chris Paul, who was also on the Clippers. When Paul was out 18 games with an injured shoulder, Collison started and averaged 13.3 points and 6.5 assists in 32.6 minutes. The Clippers went 12–6 in that span, and coach [[Doc Rivers]] said the team "weathered the storm" without their [[NBA All-Star|All-Star]] point guard; he called Collison's play "the key."{{cite news|first=Broderick|last=Turner|title=Darren Collison kept Clippers on track while Chris Paul was 2014|url-status=live|df=mdy}} ===Sacramento Kings (2014–2017)=== On July 12, 2014, Collison signed a three-year, $16 million deal with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite news|first=Arash|last=Markazi|title=Austin Rivers hitting his stride for Clippers|website=ESPN.com|publisher=ESPN|date=January 28, 7, 2015|url-status=live|df=mdy}}{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Darren Collison|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-darren-collison-0|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 12, 2014|access-date=July 12, 2014}} The Kings offered him a starting job at point guard, and the Clippers were unable to match either the deal or the playing time. On December 27, 2014, Collison had a season-best game with 27 points and 10 assists in a 135–129 overtime win over the New York Knicks.{{cite web|title=Cousins leads Kings past Knicks 135-129 in OT|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141227/NYKSAC/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 27, 2014|access-date=December 27, 2014}} On February 26, 2015, he was ruled out for three to six weeks with a right hip flexor.{{cite web|title=Darren Collison Injury Update|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/darren-collison-injury-update-2262015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 26, 2015|access-date=February 26, 2015}}{{cite 2015|access-date=February 26, 2015}} Collison was suspended for the first eight games of the 2016–17 season after pleading guilty on a misdemeanor charge of domestic battery.{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Stein|title=Kings PG Darren Collison suspended 8 games for domestic violence incident|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/17696552/darren-collison-sacramento-kings-suspended-8-games-domestic-violence-incident|work=ESPN.com|date=October 2, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}} ===Return to Indiana (2017–2019)=== On July 7, 2017, Collison signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Collison|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-collison|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}} He had knee surgery in early February 2018, returning to the Pacers' line-up in mid-March.{{cite web|title=Oladipo helps Pacers rally past Lakers 110-100|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975797|work=ESPN.com|date=March 19, 2018|access-date=March 19, 2018}} After gradually improving his three-point shooting throughout his career, Collison led the league with a career-best 47% 3-point percentage in [[2017–18 Indiana Pacers season|2017–18]].{{cite news|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|title=Sources: Darren Collison won't return to NBA this season despite interest from Lakers, Clippers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28667815/sources-darren-collison-return-nba-season-interest-lakers-clippers|website=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2020|access-date=February 11, 2020}}{{cite web|title=2017-18 NBA Leaders|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2018_leaders.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 10, 2018}} On December 10, 2018, in a 109–101 win over the [[Washington Wizards]], Collison had 17 assists, his highest single-game total with Indiana.{{cite web|title=Turner helps Pacers escape with 109-101 victory over Wizards|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071072|work=ESPN.com|date=December 10, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2018}} He ended the [[2018–19 Indiana Pacers season|2018–19 season]] with averages of 11 points and six assists. On June 28, 2019, Collison announced his retirement from the NBA. As a [[Jehovah's Witnesses|Jehovah's Witness]], he cited religious reasons for retiring.{{cite web|title=Darren Collison: 'I have decided to retire from the NBA'|url=https://andscape.com/features/darren-collison-i-have-decided-to-retire-from-the-nba/amp/|work=[[Andscape]]|date=June 28, 2019|access-date=June 28, 2019|archive-date=March 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220321141726/https://andscape.com/features/darren-collison-i-have-decided-to-retire-from-the-nba/amp/|url-status=dead}} He had been expected to draw multiple contract offers for around $10 million per season. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2021–2022)=== On December 24, 2021, Collison came out of retirement, signing a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Darren Collison to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-darren-colllison-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 24, 2021|access-date=December 25, 2021}} === South Bay Lakers (2022) === On March 24, 2022, Collison signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Darren Collison signs with Lakers' G League affiliate with hopes of getting call-up to NBA team, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/darren-collison-signs-with-lakers-g-league-affiliate-with-hopes-of-getting-call-up-to-nba-team-per-report/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=March 23, 2022 }} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#CFECEC;
